detail.abstract: Many health systems are replacing fee-for-service reimbursement with pay-for-performance (P4P), shifting the financial risk of readmissions onto hospitals. Designing such contracts is challenging for two reasons: (1) readmissions are co-produced by hospital and patient efforts;  and (2) a hospital's cost efficiency is often private. Motivated by these observations, we study a funder setting a reimbursement and a penalty where: (1) readmissions depend on two efforts via a constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) function, and (2) the hospital has one of two privately known cost types. We obtain the optimal equilibrium contract in closed form for the two special cases of the CES function: perfect substitutes and Cobb-Douglas. We also analyze the general CES case numerically. Alongside intuitive results, several findings are counterintuitive. First, the optimal menu pays the efficient hospital its informational rent through a higher reimbursement rather than a softer penalty, which flips the base-payment ranking: an efficient hospital is paid ``less'' than the inefficient rival when the funder knows costs, but it is paid "more'' when the funder does not know. Second, the cost of screening rises as care becomes more substitutable and is higher under perfect substitutes than under the Cobb-Douglas benchmark. Under complementary care, an efficient hospital gains less by pretending to be inefficient because the outcome still heavily depends on the patient's response, which ultimately reduces the information rent the funder must pay. Third, the familiar crowding-out intuition never appears: nowhere in the CES family of co-production function does the patient withdraw effort when the hospital works harder. Finally, cost information is valuable to a cost-minimizing payer because it eliminates both rent payments and screening distortions; however, it is worthless to the funder when the goal is to minimize social cost because the planner pools hospital types at the same social-cost optimal penalty.

title: Algorithmic Audit Trails for Cloud Banking Compliance: A Zero-Knowledge Proof Approach

detail.title: Algorithmic Audit Trails for Cloud Banking Compliance: A Zero-Knowledge Proof Approach
detail.abstract: This study presents a novel framework for integrating algorithmic audit trails into cloud banking compliance systems through the application of zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), addressing the critical tension between regulatory transparency and data privacy. The increasing migration of banking operations to cloud infrastructures has intensified the need for robust audit mechanisms that can verify compliance with financial regulations—such as anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) mandates—without exposing sensitive client information or proprietary risk models. Traditional audit trails, which rely on logging and storing plaintext transactional data, introduce significant vulnerabilities, including data breaches, unauthorized access, and inconsistencies across distributed cloud environments. Conversely, pure cryptographic anonymization can render audits meaningless by obscuring the provenance and integrity of records. The proposed architecture leverages ZKPs to allow an auditor (a regulatory body or internal compliance officer) to verify that a set of transactions adheres to predefined compliance rules without ever accessing the underlying data. In this system, each financial transaction executed within a cloud banking platform generates a cryptographic commitment. This commitment, along with a zero-knowledge proof, attests that the transaction satisfies all applicable regulatory constraints—such as limits on transaction value, jurisdictional restrictions, or multi-factor authentication requirements—without revealing the specific account numbers, personal identifiers, or the exact transaction details. The proof is constructed using succinct non-interactive zero-knowledge arguments (zk SNARKs), which provide both scalability and computational efficiency suitable for high-frequency transaction environments. The framework is built upon a dual-layer architecture. The first layer, the compliance engine, resides within the cloud banking application and is responsible for executing transactions, generating the corresponding ZK proofs, and committing the hashed transaction data to an immutable, decentralized ledger—a permissioned blockchain. This ledger serves as the algorithmic audit trail, recording only the cryptographic commitments and the proofs. The second layer, the audit interface, is accessible to authorized auditors. When an audit is required, the auditor submits a verification request against a specific range of transactions. The system retrieves the relevant commitments and proofs from the blockchain and runs a verification algorithm. The output is a simple Boolean result: either all transactions in the requested range are compliant, or the proof fails, triggering a detailed exception process. Importantly, the auditor gains no knowledge of the underlying transaction data; they only learn whether the regulatory predicates have been met. To realize this framework, the study identifies and addresses three principal challenges: proof generation overhead, scalability within cloud environments, and the integration of dynamic regulatory rules. Proof generation, particularly for complex compliance rules, can be computationally intensive. The proposed solution employs a hybrid approach: pre-computed proof templates for standard compliance checks (e.g., transaction size limits) are cached and reused, while complex, multi-condition checks (e.g., suspicious activity reporting rules) generate proofs on-the-fly using optimized multi-party computation techniques. For scalability, the audit trail ledger utilizes a sharded blockchain architecture, where transaction records are partitioned across multiple parallel chains based on geographic region or transaction type, ensuring that proof verification can be performed concurrently without a single bottleneck. Dynamic regulatory rules are accommodated through a modular smart contract layer. When a regulation changes, the underlying compliance predicate is updated on the blockchain, and all subsequent proofs are generated against the new rule. Existing valid proofs remain immutable, providing a historical record of compliance at the time of each transaction

title: The Resource Gadgets Pedagogical Framework: A Conceptual Model for Lecturer-guided Mobile Learning in Resource-constrained Nursing Education

detail.title: The Resource Gadgets Pedagogical Framework: A Conceptual Model for Lecturer-guided Mobile Learning in Resource-constrained Nursing Education

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: Mobile learning (m-learning)-education delivered anytime, anywhere via pocket-sized, internetconnected devices-enables nursing students to access clinical guidelines, multimedia resources, and evidence-based knowledge. Nursing education in resource-constrained low-and middleincome countries (LMICs) faces a persistent paradox: simulation laboratories, audiovisual equipment, and institutional WiFi remain largely inaccessible, yet university-enrolled students almost universally own internet-enabled smartphones. M-learning offers a scalable, zeroinfrastructure pedagogical response; however, no named, theorized, or replicable framework exists to guide lecturer-directed, device-based classroom pedagogy in these settings. This conceptual paper develops and operationalizes the Resource Gadgets Pedagogical Framework, the first theorized, replicable model for structured smartphone use in resourceconstrained nursing classrooms. The framework synthesizes qualitative evidence from undergraduate nursing students in sub-Saharan Africa with six complementary learning theories: social constructivism, andragogy, Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning, Activity Theory, critical pedagogy, and Self-Determination Theory. The Resource Gadgets Pedagogical Framework conceptualizes lecturer-guided smartphone-mediated learning as a structured five-component instructional cycle: (1) Structured Initiation, (2) Guided Digital Inquiry, (3) Visual-Multimodal Processing, (4) Collaborative Synthesis, and (5) Educator-Facilitated Anchoring; each theoretically anchored and operationalized through practical classroom strategies without institutional technology investment. The Resource Gadgets Pedagogical Framework (RGPF) reframes the student smartphone from a perceived classroom distraction into a structured cognitive learning tool, embeds digital equity safeguards as non-negotiable implementation conditions, and positions m-learning as a gateway toward AI-enhanced nursing education. The RGPF offers educators, curriculum designers, and policymakers a citable, empirically grounded foundation for lecturer-guided mobile-assisted learning, curriculum innovation, and future empirical validation across diverse global nursing education contexts.

title: Using Healthcare Data Analytics to Detect Healthcare Fraud in the United States
affiliations: Brandeis University

detail.title: Using Healthcare Data Analytics to Detect Healthcare Fraud in the United States

detail.abstract: Healthcare fraud remains one of the most persistent threats to the financial sustainability and integrity of the United States healthcare system. Fraudulent activities contribute to billions of dollars in annual losses, divert critical resources away from patient care, and undermine public trust in healthcare institutions. Federal agencies, including the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the Government Accountability Office (GAO), and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG), have identified healthcare fraud, improper payments, and program integrity challenges as ongoing threats to the effectiveness of public healthcare programs (CMS, 2024; GAO, 2025; HHS-OIG, 2024). Advances in healthcare data analytics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence have created new opportunities to identify suspicious billing patterns and support proactive fraud prevention efforts (Rajkomar et al., 2019; Beam & Kohane, 2018). This study examined the role of predictive analytics in detecting potentially fraudulent healthcare providers using a publicly available U.S. healthcare claims dataset containing fraud labels. Provider-level claims characteristics were derived from inpatient and outpatient claims data and linked to fraud status. Descriptive analyses, independent samples t-tests, logistic regression, and Random Forest classification models were employed to identify factors associated with fraud and evaluate predictive performance. Of 5,410 providers included in the analysis, 9.4% were classified as potentially fraudulent. Fraudulent providers submitted substantially more claims (63.7 vs. 8.5 claims) and received significantly higher reimbursements ($304,377 vs. $22,707) than nonfraudulent providers (p < 0.001). A Random Forest model achieved 92.4% overall classification accuracy and identified reimbursement patterns as the strongest predictor of fraud. These findings demonstrate the potential of healthcare analytics to strengthen fraud detection and support more efficient allocation of investigative resources. The study highlights the importance of integrating predictive analytics into healthcare program integrity efforts and demonstrates the value of datadriven approaches for strengthening healthcare fraud prevention.

title: Rising Inequality from AI Job Loss: A Dystopian Reality that We Have the Chance to Avoid
affiliations: MIT Media Lab - Digital Currency Initiative

detail.title: Rising Inequality from AI Job Loss: A Dystopian Reality that We Have the Chance to Avoid
detail.abstract: There is no doubt that AI is coming for some jobs, but the overwhelming question is-who is most at-risk of job loss and how long is the pain going to last? Are Amazon warehouse workers first in line for job loss or are the consultants, software developers, and financial analysts going to feel the pain of the first wave? A new consensus is emerging that focuses on jobs "exposed to AI" and identifying workers who have the skills to land back on their feet when AI comes knocking at their door. New data analysis of these AI-exposed jobs reveals that there are 3 categories of workers who face the biggest threats from this technological shift. Regardless of the worker category though, there's a more sinister inequality that is taking shape.

title: Target-Based Linear–Quadratic Investment and Spending for Endowment Funds under Jump-Driven Donation Risk
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Brescia and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Target-Based Linear–Quadratic Investment and Spending for Endowment Funds under Jump-Driven Donation Risk
detail.abstract: In this paper, we study the long-term investment and spending problem of an endowment fund that seeks to stabilise its spending around a desired target while facing uncertain financial markets and jump-driven donation income. Endowment funds are long-term institutional investors, similar to pension funds, and their joint management of investment and spending constitutes a target-based asset–liability problem of direct actuarial interest. The exogenous donation flow is modelled through a Poisson process with random, market-correlated jump sizes, asset dynamics follow a Geometric Brownian Motion, and the fund minimises a quadratic loss that penalises deviations of both consumption and wealth from dynamically evolving benchmarks. We formulate the associated continuous-time linear–quadratic stochastic control problem and solve it through the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation, obtaining closed-form optimal consumption and investment policies—an explicit Riccati solution for the wealth-curvature coefficient complemented by one-dimensional quadratures for the remaining coefficients—that balance sustainability with stability. A central ingredient is a mobile target that adjusts endogenously to incoming Poisson shocks, which prevents the pathological strategies that arise when income shocks are evaluated against a fixed benchmark. We develop the framework with endowment funds as the leading application, calibrating it on the Harvard University endowment over the period 2007–2024. The target-based formulation and the treatment of Poisson-driven income are, however, general: they can be adapted to other long-horizon institutional funds, most notably defined-contribution pension schemes and the decumulation phase, as well as to insurance asset–liability management under stochastic contribution and liability flows.

title: Nutritional Status Trajectories and Academic Performance: Longitudinal Evidence from Chile
affiliations: University of Chile, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Duke University

detail.title: Nutritional Status Trajectories and Academic Performance: Longitudinal Evidence from Chile
detail.abstract: Chile ranks among the highest in the OECD for overweight and obesity prevalence, with over half of school-age children affected — yet no prior study has examined the consequences for academic outcomes in this context. This paper investigates how longitudinal trajectories of nutritional status from early childhood to adolescence affect academic performance among Chilean students. Using a census-level panel dataset of 78,893 students observed in first, fifth, and ninth grade between 2014 and 2022, we construct eight nutritional status trajectory categories — ranging from persistently normal to persistently affected by overweight or obesity (OwOb) — and estimate their association with ninth-grade percentile ranking and school attendance. Identification relies on school fixed effects and lagged dependent variables to control for unobserved school-level heterogeneity and prior academic trends. We find that transitioning into OwOb during adolescence reduces girls’ percentile ranking by 1.2 points and attendance by 0.45 percentage points relative to peers who maintained normal nutritional status throughout. Transitions into obesity specifically carry the largest penalties: girls who become obese during adolescence experience a decline of over 3 percentile points in academic ranking. Conversely, exiting OwOb states is associated with significant academic improvements for both sexes, with gains of up to 2.4 percentile points for girls and 1.7 for boys. Effects are consistently larger when the nutritional transition involves obesity rather than overweight, and are more pronounced during adolescence than childhood. Robustness checks using SIMCE standardized test scores confirm the direction and magnitude of the main findings. These results suggest that the educational costs of childhood obesity are substantial, gender-differentiated, and sensitive to the timing and severity of nutritional transitions — underscoring the value of early, sustained interventions targeting nutritional health in school-age populations.

title: Closed Without Warning: Material Marginalization of People in the Sex Trades

declarations.ethicsApproval: In addition to IRB approval through Cornell University, the research team included ethical standards upheld by participatory research, such as consultation and iterative feedback throughout the process with the community being studied. While the ethics of sex workers provided additional guidelines, such as avoiding extractive and exploitative practices often seen in institutions, we still chose to go through the process of IRB approval through Cornell to be able to share our research and findings in institutional spaces where we hope there is a greater chance of policy changes.

detail.abstract: The exclusion of sex workers from financial services raises critical concerns about justice, autonomy, and economic rights. Sex workers report increased vulnerability and violence due to difficulties accessing banking and financial technologies. This paper examines how algorithms used by financial institutions de-platform individuals engaged in sex work under the pretense of risk management, regardless of the legal status of their labor. Using mixed-methods analysis, this study demonstrates that financial discrimination experienced by sex workers leads to housing instability, food insecurity, and broader health and safety challenges. This study employs community-led participatory action research to gather data from individuals involved in the sex trades, documenting their experiences of financial discrimination and the resulting impacts on their lives; 32% of respondents have been banned from a bank account, payment app, or payment processor, 23% reported having funds seized, and financial discrimination increased the longer respondents engaged in sex work.

title: The Enigma of Ticket Exchanges (and Other Reselling Markets) and the Design of Commission Fees
affiliations: The Wharton School - Operations, Information and Decisions Department and University of Virginia - Darden School of Business

detail.title: The Enigma of Ticket Exchanges (and Other Reselling Markets) and the Design of Commission Fees
detail.abstract: The literature establishes (and practice confirms) that sellers can benefit from allowing consumers to purchase in advance of the date of actual consumption (e.g., concert tickets, sporting events, etc.). Because of this advance purchasing, consumers can find themselves either with a ticket that they no longer want, or without a ticket that they wish to have. In the past, scalpers would facilitate transactions among these consumers, for a fee. Sellers historically disliked those practices and actively worked to prevent them. In fact, we obtain a stark finding: an unfettered and efficient reselling market eliminates all of the benefits of advance selling, which justifies sellers' historic hostility to reselling. But now ticket exchanges are common, growing, and even embraced by sellers. What changed? We present a theory that demonstrates reselling is actually beneficial for sellers under one crucial condition-the seller must have some control over the reselling process, thereby allowing the seller to earn something from each transaction through commission fees. The old-fashioned paper ticket did not give such control, but technology now enables electronic tickets, which do. In fact, a seller cannot earn more than what it receives from a properly designed reselling market (i.e., reselling is optimal for the seller), especially for popular events with limited capacity. When market demand is uncertain, the optimal commission should vary with the demand state, which may be challenging to implement in practice. Fortunately, seller revenue is strong even with a single commission rate, and captures nearly all of the achievable revenue if combined with a cap on collected commissions. However, while authorized reselling increase overall social welfare because it corrects the allocation errors inherent in advance selling, consumer surplus is always greater with an uncontrolled reselling market. In sum, our results explain why the seller's view towards reselling has shifted dramatically, we illuminate the welfare tradeoffs this shift entails, and provide simple and effective commission structures.

detail.abstract: FIFA stands for Fédération Internationale de Football Association (French for International Federation of Association Football). FIFA World Cup is a major event on worldwide scene. As the 2026 edition is coming to North America, it is worth looking at several perspectives. Finances of FIFA is an important dimension.  FIFA’s financial architecture sits at the center of one of the world’s most influential sporting ecosystems, yet it remains a subject of persistent scrutiny and debate. As the governing body responsible for organizing global competitions and distributing billions of dollars across national associations, FIFA operates within a complex network of revenue streams, expenses allocation, and accountability mechanisms.  The study aims to analyze key elements of FIFA’s financial operations in its capacity as the primary organizer of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Drawing on five years of financial data, it seeks to outline FIFA’s financial profile and develop a deeper understanding of how the organization manages and allocates its resources. An appendix is included, providing a table of contents and an index of tables.

title: A Monte Carlo Heuristic Framework for Finite-Horizon Inventory Optimization Under Stochastic Demand with Deterioration
affiliations: Vidyasagar University - Tamralipta Mahavidyalaya

detail.title: A Monte Carlo Heuristic Framework for Finite-Horizon Inventory Optimization Under Stochastic Demand with Deterioration
detail.abstract: This study develops a generalized finite-horizon inventory model that integrates complex demand patterns, deterioration, seasonal effects, and stochastic variability within a Monte Carlo-based simulation framework in MATLAB. The model incorporates fixed, holding, procurement, deterioration, transportation, backordering, and lost sales costs, enabling comprehensive cost evaluation. Simulation results show that deterioration and seasonality significantly affect optimal replenishment cycles and order quantities, and that the model yields robust cost estimates under uncertainty. Sensitivity analysis further indicates that the base demand rate has the strongest effect on cost outcomes, followed by procurement and backorder costs, whereas seasonality and holding cost parameters exhibit negligible influence.

title: Intellectual Theft In Nigeria: Piracy And Counterfeit As Case Study

detail.title: Intellectual Theft In Nigeria: Piracy And Counterfeit As Case Study
detail.abstract: The landscape of intellectual property rights in Nigeria has been significantly impacted by the pervasive issues of piracy and counterfeiting. This paper delved into the intricate dynamics of intellectual theft in the country, focusing primarily on piracy and counterfeiting as emblematic case studies. In Nigeria's diverse marketplaces and digital spheres, rampant piracy persists, wherein copyrighted material such as movies, music, software, and literature are illicitly reproduced and distributed without authorization. Additionally, the proliferation of counterfeit goods, ranging from pharmaceuticals to luxury products, undermines both local and international businesses, impacting economic growth and public health. The paper examined the types of piracy and counterfeiting and how they manifest in various forms. Further, the paper explored the prevalence of piracy and counterfeiting in Nigeria stemming from a combination of factors, including weak intellectual property laws, inadequate enforcement mechanisms, high poverty levels, and a lack of public awareness. The study found out that these illicit activities have farreaching consequences, undermining innovation, stifling creativity, and endangering consumer safety. The study posited that Nigeria has enacted various laws to address intellectual property theft and that these laws are complemented by legal institutions. However, while the legal and institutional measures exist, their effectiveness in combating piracy and counterfeiting remains limited. To curb these illicit activities, the study proposed strategic frameworks for combatting intellectual theft in Nigeria through legislative reinforcement, enhanced enforcement mechanisms, and public awareness campaigns to safeguard creators' rights and foster a culture of respect for intellectual property.

detail.abstract: FIFA stands for Fédération Internationale de Football Association (French for International Federation of Association Football). The 2026 FIFA World Cup is a landmark event on the world stage, bringing together three host nations, Canada, Mexico, and the United States, for the first tri-nation tournament in the competition's history. As preparations accelerate and public debate intensifies, the World Cup has become more than a sporting spectacle: it is a catalyst for political negotiation, economic planning, cultural expression, and social transformation across North America. Governments, cities, corporations, and institutions are all working to leverage the tournament's visibility and economic potential, while navigating the controversies, expectations, and pressures that accompany a mega-event of this scale. This study examines the 2026 FIFA World Cup through its key dimensions and controversies, with the goal of deepening our understanding of the event. Drawing on a Canadian perspective, it explores how the tournament both shapes and is shaped by the political, economic, financial, ecological, social, and cultural dynamics of its host countries.

title: A Strategic Transformation Framework for Pakistan Television Corporation (PTV)
affiliations: National Defence University and National Defence University

detail.title: A Strategic Transformation Framework for Pakistan Television Corporation (PTV)
detail.abstract: Pakistan Television Corporation (PTV), the country's state-owned national broadcaster established in 1964, occupies a historically significant yet strategically precarious position in Pakistan's rapidly evolving media landscape. This case study presents a structured organizational analysis of PTV's digital transition challenges, drawing on documentary research, comparative broadcaster studies, and strategic management theory. The study proposes an original contribution-the PTV Digital Transformation Model (PDTM)-a five-stage sequential framework tailored to the institutional realities of public-sector broadcasters navigating competitive digital markets. The analysis identifies rigid governance architecture, insufficient investment in innovation capacity, and the absence of a coherent multi-platform strategy as the core impediments to PTV's competitive renewal. To address these challenges, the study argues that sustainable performance requires the deliberate alignment of three interdependent forces: leadership agility, technology-enabled content delivery, and diversified digital revenue. The PDTM is designed with sufficient conceptual generalizability to serve as a strategic tool for comparable state-owned media institutions across developing economies.

title: Venture Capital and Scientists' Selection into Entrepreneurship

detail.title: Venture Capital and Scientists' Selection into Entrepreneurship
detail.abstract: Using newly digitized historical data on over 450,000 U.S. scientists, this paper examines whether venture capital (VC) facilitates commercialization through new business formation. I exploit the "prudent man" rule reform as a quasi-natural experiment that increased VC supply. Scientists in intangible-intensive specialties, who were ex ante more likely to benefit from VC, experienced a 21% relative increase in business formation, concentrated in counties with VC presence. Among private-sector, high-wage, and patenting scientists, the relative increase was as high as fivefold. These individual-level effects contributed to county-level growth in intangible industries and persisted through the end of the sample period.

title: Book Review: Optimising Public Interests through Competitive Tendering: Concept, Context and Challenges, by Chris Jansen, Frank van Ommeren, Johan Wolswinkel and Sue Arrowsmith, (Cambridge University Press, 2025).
affiliations: University of Dayton

detail.title: Book Review: Optimising Public Interests through Competitive Tendering: Concept, Context and Challenges, by Chris Jansen, Frank van Ommeren, Johan Wolswinkel and Sue Arrowsmith, (Cambridge University Press, 2025).
detail.abstract:
Public procurement, licensing, subsidies, and sales are kindred subjects whose disciplinary isolation imposes real costs. This volume vindicates that premise with unusual rigor and coherence. The review highlights three chapters of particular interest to procurement scholars: Sue Arrowsmith's magisterial treatment of public procurement, characterized here as the book's disciplinary lodestar, which offers perhaps the most comprehensive account of procurement's diverse objectives yet written; Chapter 6's nuanced argument that concessions and procurement are conceptually distinct domains warranting bespoke regulatory solutions; and the concluding chapter's synthesis of cross-domain lessons, including the centrality of transparency as a precondition for competitive allocation. The review also notes the book's treatment of the performance phase, the analogies and disanalogies between procurement and government sales, and the limits of procurement as a legal transplant. While some chapters presuppose deep familiarity with EU law, the collection as a whole is essential reading for procurement scholars and practitioners alike.

This review was originally published in Public Procurement Law Review, published by Thomson Reuters (Sweet & Maxwell). The author gratefully acknowledges Thomson Reuters for its generosity in permitting the posting of this work on SSRN, and thanks the editors for their stewardship of this important journal.

title: Velocity with Containment: An AI Adoption Doctrine for Mid-Market Leaders

detail.title: Velocity with Containment: An AI Adoption Doctrine for Mid-Market Leaders

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of The Brained Inc., an independent advisory firm that works with mid-market companies and investors on AI strategy. This document reflects the author's own analysis and is not written on behalf of, or sponsored by, any vendor or client. No third party reviewed or approved its content.
declarations.funderStatement: This work received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Mid-market companies have adopted AI almost universally and have, almost as universally, struggled to show what it was worth. This document explains the gap and offers a way across it. The argument is that the mid-market holds a genuine structural advantage in AI adoption: decision velocity, the ability to move from a decision to a live system while a larger rival is still scheduling the meeting. Most firms destroy that advantage by imitating the enterprise, importing its governance, its roadmaps, and its coordination overhead along with its slowness. The discipline that preserves the advantage is containment: holding that speed inside two deliberate guardrails, a clearly defined business goal and a realistic grasp of recurring cost.


The deeper claim is that the determinant of success is not technology but the human layer. Motivated, capable, involved people are what turn a working tool into a working capability, and AI-native people are the precondition for an AI-native company. The document gives C-level leaders of US mid-market firms a strategic frame for making the adoption decision well, before governance and before tooling, and leaves the execution to leaders who, once they are thinking clearly, are entirely capable of it. It is a doctrine, not a manual: it supplies the distinctions and the small number of load-bearing ideas that make a good decision possible, and ends each chapter on a single question the reader must answer for their own company. Its argument is organized around a set of original frameworks developed by the author, including the Motivation Taxonomy, the Imitation Trap, and Velocity with Containment.

title: 30 Years of Research on Income Shifting—Review and Looking Ahead
affiliations: and University of Waterloo - School of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: 30 Years of Research on Income Shifting—Review and Looking Ahead
detail.abstract: This paper provides a structured survey of the empirical literature on the taxmotivated income-shifting behavior of multinational corporations (MNCs). Tax-motivated income shifting refers to a set of tax planning strategies used by MNCs to lower their global tax burden by strategically reporting their taxable profits in tax-preferrable jurisdictions. This study fills a gap in the existing knowledge of international tax research by (1) exploring this very broad literature using structured methods to identify income shifting papers, and (2) focusing specifically on the sizable literature on mechanisms, determinants including internal and external firm factors, consequences, and estimated magnitudes of income shifting. This survey contributes to the literature by organizing and summarizing what has been learned about income shifting, and highlighting areas where future income-shifting research is needed. We organize our recommendations into three key areas: opportunities to enhance the methods for estimating income shifting; understudied areas observed from our review of income shifting mechanisms, determinants, consequences, and magnitudes; and guidance specific to doctoral students interested in doing income shifting research.

title: Softening the Blow: The Role of Environmental Communication following Product Recalls
affiliations: University of St Andrews Business School, University of Graz and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Softening the Blow: The Role of Environmental Communication following Product Recalls
detail.abstract: We examine how environmental communication via corporate social media affects the equity returns of firms around adverse product-market events. Product recalls expose firms to significant reputational damage and reductions in shareholder value. Prior literature demonstrates that investors value sustainability narratives, incorporating them into investment decisions and positively pricing environmental disclosures. Consequently, during crises, managers have strong incentives to shape investor perceptions by disseminating positive environmental narratives. Using a sample of product incidents and Twitter activity for international automotive firms, we employ an instrumental variable approach to isolate the impact of this communication. We find that firms engaging in environmental tweeting, immediately following a product recall, experience significantly less negative abnormal returns. This mitigating effect is specific to environmental content; general increases in social media volume yield no such benefit. The effect is substantially stronger when firms deploy specific, action-oriented environmental messages rather than generic sustainability claims. This strategic communication channel has become effective primarily in the post-2016 period, consistent with a shift in investor attention toward ESG commitments following the Paris Agreement.

title: Monetary Policy, Financial Architecture, and Competition
affiliations: Imperial College London

detail.title: Monetary Policy, Financial Architecture, and Competition
detail.abstract: I examine how monetary policy shapes competition through financial architecture. Exploiting a classic measure of product closeness between firms, I show that monetary tightening induces convergence in a Hotelling-like product space, intensifying horizontal competition, with the strongest effects among the closest and reciprocally important competitors. Consistent with financing-based explanations, firms with access to nonbank credit exhibit significantly weaker convergence responses. These effects are not easily attributable to market-based explanations. The findings suggest that competition is endogenous to monetary policy and highlight the role of financial architecture, through nonbank finance, in conditioning the real effects of monetary policy.

title: A Theory of Sequential Decision Making
affiliations: Universita di Chieti Pescara

detail.title: A Theory of Sequential Decision Making
detail.abstract: An agent who cannot evaluate all payo¤-relevant evidence simultaneously must choose how to organise it before sequential inspection begins. This paper studies the choice of that organisation. Before evaluation, the agent selects a sign-coherent partition of the state space and orders its blocks by the strength of their payo¤-relevant content; the resulting sequential decision structure determines how rapidly decisive evidence accumulates and therefore how fast and how reliably a decision is reached. Every representation induces two evaluative properties-evidential concentration and payo¤ discrimination-that generically con-‡ict, and the paper develops a classi…cation of evaluative environments organised around this trade-o¤. The analysis proceeds through three progressively endogenised environments: a hard capacity bound, a per-block attention cost, and a one-time acquisition cost amortised over repeated use. Admissible maximisers lie on the concentration-discrimination frontier; the environment taxonomy-alignment, con ‡ict, and the polar regimes of uniform evidential dominance and uniform re…nement dominance-classi…es decision problems by whether the trade-o¤ is present, absent, or resolved by primitives. Endogenous heterogeneity in representational re…nement arises through expected reuse value. Speed and accuracy depend on the organisation of evidence as well as on the stopping threshold.

title: Equity Ethics: The Racialized Logic of Entrepreneurial Motivation
affiliations: , St. John's University Tobin College of Business and Johns Hopkins University

detail.title: Equity Ethics: The Racialized Logic of Entrepreneurial Motivation
detail.abstract: Mainstream entrepreneurship theory posits that venture creation is primarily driven by the recognition of economic opportunities; however, we find that for underrepresented and racially minoritized (URM) founders, a different logic, one rooted in equity ethics and the moral intensity of lived experience, can operate as an equally, if not more, powerful driver. Using survey data from over 600 STEM-trained founders, we find that URM founders in the United States are significantly more likely to pursue ventures offering products and services that target marginalized populations than their non-URM counterparts. This relationship is substantially mediated by the founders' own racialized experiences, including racial activism and higher levels of equity ethics-a worldview that converts experience with injustice into a professional imperative. Furthermore, even among founders of ventures serving marginalized groups, URM founders report more intense racialized motivations. By centering race as an antecedent, this study theorizes and provides evidence for an alternative pathway to entrepreneurship, one rooted in redress and racial justice, with significant implications for entrepreneurial theory, pedagogy, and ecosystem design.

title: Governing Innovation Beyond the Quarterly Cycle: A Systems-Based Architecture for Long-Horizon Value Creation

detail.title: Governing Innovation Beyond the Quarterly Cycle: A Systems-Based Architecture for Long-Horizon Value Creation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that no personal, financial, or organisational conflict of interest has influenced the development of this technical report. The conceptual mod-els and frameworks presented are original intellectual property developed as part of Rosemonte Ltd.’s strategic leadership research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research and the development of the associated frameworks were fully self-funded by Rosemonte Limited. No external funding, grants, or institutional sponsorship were received.
declarations.funderStatement: This research and the development of the associated governance frameworks were fully funded and undertaken within Rosemonte Ltd. as part of its Executive Series research and advisory programme. The work reflects internally directed research priorities aligned with Rosemonte’s leadership and systems architecture practice across complex industrial and capital-intensive environments.

detail.abstract: The ability to develop, preserve, renew, and deploy organisational capabilities has emerged as a central challenge for enterprises operating within environments shaped by technological disruption, sustainability transitions, geopolitical fragmentation, artificial intelligence, stakeholder scrutiny, and evolving regulatory expectations. Whilst governance research has traditionally focused upon ownership structures, accountability mechanisms, and board oversight, innovation scholarship has concentrated upon technological development, dynamic capabilities, and organisational adaptation. Similarly, sustainability research has largely emphasised reporting frameworks, disclosure systems, and stakeholder accountability. Despite these contributions, limited attention has been directed towards understanding how organisations systematically create capabilities before markets, technologies, regulatory systems, and stakeholder expectations fully mature. This paper develops an Enterprise Stewardship Architecture™ that integrates governance, stewardship, capital allocation, capability development, legitimacy management, stakeholder architectures, and adaptive capacity within a unified systems-based perspective. Drawing upon stewardship theory, stakeholder theory, dynamic capabilities, systems architecture, and engineering systems scholarship, the paper advances the concepts of Long-Horizon Value Creation Capacity™ and Capability Economics to explain how organisations sustain strategic continuity whilst investing in capabilities whose value may not be immediately visible through conventional financial metrics. Particular attention is directed towards the governance challenge of balancing present performance with future preparedness, recognising that many strategically significant capabilities require sustained investment long before competitive necessity becomes apparent. The Feadship × LVMH Breakthrough programme is examined as an illustrative case through which these dynamics may be explored. Rather than evaluating technological performance alone, the study investigates the governance conditions required to support capability development, stakeholder legitimacy, regulatory engagement, ecosystem coordination, and long-horizon innovation. The analysis demonstrates that the significance of Breakthrough extends beyond hydrogen propulsion technology, providing insight into how organisations preserve specialised expertise, cultivate stakeholder trust, coordinate strategic partnerships, and invest in future capability architectures under conditions of technological and institutional transition. The paper contributes to governance research by extending conventional perspectives beyond oversight and control towards a systems-based understanding of enterprise stewardship, capability development, and long-term value creation. It introduces the Five Interacting Horizons Framework™, Enterprise Capability Development Architecture™, and Enterprise Stewardship Architecture™ as complementary mechanisms for understanding how organisations create, preserve, renew, and deploy capabilities across extended temporal horizons. The study further argues that ESG outcomes are more appropriately understood as emergent properties of governance architecture rather than standalone reporting mechanisms. The resulting framework provides both a conceptual and practical foundation for evaluating organisational resilience, strategic continuity, capability development, and long-horizon innovation across advanced manufacturing, aerospace, maritime, luxury, technology, and family-controlled enterprises.

title: Governing the Loop: A Critical Examination of AI-Driven Digital Twin Frameworks for Circular Economy Optimization in Smart Manufacturing Systems

detail.title: Governing the Loop: A Critical Examination of AI-Driven Digital Twin Frameworks for Circular Economy Optimization in Smart Manufacturing Systems
detail.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence, digital twin technology, and circular economy principles has generated substantial scholarly and industrial interest, yet the governance mechanisms required to operationalize these systems remain undertheorized. This paper critically examines the extent to which AI-driven digital twin frameworks can effectively optimize material flows, product life cycles, and reverse logistics within smart manufacturing environments. Drawing on a qualitative meta-synthesis of peer-reviewed case studies (2019-2025) and a thematic analysis of technical architecture documents from fourteen manufacturing firms, the study identifies a persistent decoupling between real-time data integration and long-term circularity metrics. Findings indicate that while digital twins excel at predictive maintenance and process efficiency, their contribution to circular objectives such as remanufacturing, material traceability, and design for disassembly remains contingent upon institutional alignment, data interoperability standards, and regulatory incentives. The paper advances a conceptual model-the Circular Digital Twin Governance Framework-which integrates technical fidelity with stakeholder accountability. Key contributions include a typology of four governance archetypes (reactive, responsive, adaptive, and regenerative) and a critical assessment of current implementation barriers. The study concludes that without deliberate policy interventions and cross-sector data governance, AI-driven digital twins risk reinforcing linear production logics rather than enabling circular transitions. Implications for industrial ecology, manufacturing policy, and sustainable systems design are discussed.

title: Behavioural, Structural and Leadership Interventions for Organisational Sustainability Transitions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Behavioural, Structural and Leadership Interventions for Organisational Sustainability Transitions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest

detail.abstract: Despite growing institutional pressure, organisations continue to struggle with translating sustainability intentions into lasting behavioural change. This paper argues that single-layer interventions, most commonly training, are insufficient for meaningful sustainability transitions. Drawing on behavioural science, organisational theory, and leadership research, this paper develops an integrated multi-level framework that synthesises individual-level behavioural mechanisms, social and leadership enablers, and structural and organisational conditions. The COM-B model (Michie et al., 2011) serves as the integrative lens, mapping onto three interconnected levels at which barriers to sustainable decision-making operate. The framework positions ethical and sustainable decision-making as the target organisational behaviour and identifies the conditions under which multi-level interventions can embed this behaviour as a consistent organisational practice.

title:
The Acquisition of Brains under Antitrust Scrutiny in Brazil: Acqui-Hiring, The Microsoft/Inflection AI
Case, and the New Competition Challenges in Artificial Intelligence Markets
affiliations: Universidade de Brasília (UnB) and Lefosse Lawyers

detail.title:
The Acquisition of Brains under Antitrust Scrutiny in Brazil: Acqui-Hiring, The Microsoft/Inflection AI
Case, and the New Competition Challenges in Artificial Intelligence Markets
detail.abstract: This article examines the antitrust implications of acqui-hiring - a corporate strategy of acquiring companies primarily to absorb their skilled human capital - in light of the Brazilian Administrative Council for Economic Defense's (CADE) recent decision to call in the Microsoft/Inflection AI transaction in June 2026. Although the transaction was initially characterized as mere employee hiring and did not meet Brazil's traditional revenue thresholds for mandatory notification, CADE's Tribunal ordered the parties to submit it for review, signaling a shift toward a substance-over-form approach in merger control. The paper analyzes the competitive risks associated with acqui-hiring and at the same time, the article acknowledges the pro-competitive effects of such arrangements, such as innovation acceleration, efficient talent reallocation, and synergies. Drawing on international precedents, the paper situates CADE's decision within a broader global trend of increased scrutiny over transactions involving the transfer of strategic personnel, particularly in innovation-intensive sectors such as artificial intelligence.

title: Serial Entrepreneurship: Rethinking Top Wealth Dynamics
affiliations: Brown University, Le Mans University and Le Mans University

detail.title: Serial Entrepreneurship: Rethinking Top Wealth Dynamics
detail.abstract: This paper uncovers novel facts about serial entrepreneurship at the top of the wealth distribution. While business ownership is prevalent among the richest households, top business wealth is not simply built by scaling a single large firm. In the SCF, business-owning households in the top 0.1 percent own about seven private businesses on average, while Forbes-listed individuals own around ten. These portfolios are active and dynamic. Entrepreneurs enter new ventures, scale some of them, close or sell others, and reallocate capital across them. Private equity returns fall sharply with wealth for single-firm owners, but much less for entrepreneurs with multiple firms. We develop a tractable general equilibrium theory in which entrepreneurs operate multiple firms subject to decreasing returns and search for high-yield opportunities. The model matches the concentration of multi-firm entrepreneurs at the top, the flows into and out of multi-firm ownership, and the flatter returnwealth profile among rich households. Wealth taxation has ambiguous effects. It improves selection toward high-return entrepreneurs, but weakens experimentation at the top.

title: Confidence Laundering: How AI Systems Transform Uncertainty into Authority
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Confidence Laundering: How AI Systems Transform Uncertainty into Authority
detail.abstract: AI systems are increasingly embedded in decisions that allocate credit, employment, and other economic opportunities. In these settings, decision-makers rarely see raw model outputs. They see summaries-reports, dashboards, or generated narratives-that translate probabilistic signals into apparent conclusions. In this translation, something critical is often lost: the uncertainty itself. This paper names and analyzes this pattern as confidence laundering-the process by which AI systems transform uncertain, inferred, or probabilistic information into outputs that are perceived as high-confidence or deterministic. While prior work has documented miscalibration within models (Guo et al., 2017; Kuleshov et al., 2018) and AI-driven over-reliance in human decision-makers (Buccìnca et al., 2021; Vasconcelos et al., 2023), less attention has been paid to the structural mechanisms by which uncertainty is removed between model output and institutional action. This paper documents three such mechanisms-linguistic compression at the summarization layer, visual override through pre-attentive confidence signals, and diffusion of epistemic responsibility across pipeline stagesand argues that confidence laundering is a pipeline property, not a model property, with implications for how AI governance frameworks are designed and applied.

title: Cumulative Asset Purchase Announcements Are Not Useful to Quantify Quantitative Easing in SVAR Models
affiliations: University of the German Federal Armed Forces - Helmut Schmidt Universität

detail.title: Cumulative Asset Purchase Announcements Are Not Useful to Quantify Quantitative Easing in SVAR Models
detail.abstract: While cumulative asset purchase announcement (APA) series have been studied by means of structural vector autoregressive (SVAR) models to analyze the macroeconomic effects of quantitative easing (QE) since the influential study by Weale & Wieladek (2016), I demonstrate that resulting estimates are unreliable. First, I show that a cumulative APA series captures only a very small subset of central bank communication events to highlight its degenerate information structure. This lack of information is confirmed by means of statistical tests suggesting that sign restrictions on a cumulative APA series are highly unlikely to contribute meaningfully to the identification of QE shocks. Rather, the SVAR residuals are contaminated by arbitrary noise due to the piecewise-constant step-function shape of the cumulative APA series obscuring the signal provided by announcements. Second, I show that the main U.S. result of Weale & Wieladek (2016) is subject to an omitted variable bias because they construct their cumulative APA series in a way that is not well grounded on economic facts.

title: Wetware Intelligence and the Law of Living Computation Functional Coupling and the Governance of Bio-Digital Neural Substrates

detail.title: Wetware Intelligence and the Law of Living Computation Functional Coupling and the Governance of Bio-Digital Neural Substrates

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not applicable.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Self funded.

detail.abstract:
This working paper develops a substrate-sensitive legal and technical framework for governing living computational systems. Its central claim is that the relevant legal threshold should not be sentience, personhood, commercial usefulness or mere biological responsiveness. The threshold should be functional coupling: the condition in which living neural tissue materially alters the behaviour of a computational system through measurable, task-relevant, state-dependent dynamics. The paper therefore treats remotely accessible wetware platforms not as replacements for GPUs, nor as speculative proto-persons, but as bio-digital neural substrates whose regulatory character arises from the integration of human-derived or animal-derived neural cells, stimulation hardware, signalprocessing software, cloud interfaces, platform contracts, data pipelines and downstream computational use.
The analysis reconstructs two early architectural families. FinalSpark’s Neuroplatform uses threedimensional forebrain organoids on multi-electrode arrays, with continuous electrophysiological monitoring, remote Python access, spike recording, microfluidic support and accumulated neuronalactivity datasets. Cortical Labs’ DishBrain and CL1 systems use planar neuronal cultures grown across silicon interfaces and embedded in real-time closed-loop environments. The contrast matters because morphology changes legal risk: three-dimensional organoids foreground provenance, welfare, diffusion and lifecycle problems, while planar cultures foreground latency, controllability, deployment and closed-loop agency risks.

title: Provident Development Studies: Reframing Development Around the Structural Continuity of Human Agency
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Provident Development Studies: Reframing Development Around the Structural Continuity of Human Agency
detail.abstract: Development Studies has expanded beyond income, growth, and welfare toward capabilities, institutions, sustainability, and multidimensional wellbeing. Yet a central question remains insufficiently foregrounded: whether societies preserve the structural conditions under which dignified human agency can remain credible across generations. A society may improve present indicators of income, education, health, infrastructure, and governance while weakening the demographic, institutional, monetary, cognitive, ecological, bodily, and moral conditions that make long-horizon agency possible. Such a society may be running an intergenerational deficit: present welfare is being maintained by drawing down the structures required to sustain it. This article proposes Provident Development Studies as a programmatic reorientation of the field. Drawing on the Providence Value Unit framework, it argues that development should be evaluated not only by present outcomes or present capabilities, but by the structural reproducibility of meaningful agency across time. The article specifies how this object differs from its nearest neighbours: sustainable human development, inclusive wealth, resilience, and social reproduction. It also offers explicit criteria for what counts as an agency-continuity condition, together with the evidence that would count against the framework. It develops five claims. First, Development Studies should treat agency continuity as a central evaluative object. Second, it should distinguish present capability from the systems that reproduce capability. Third, it should treat development pillars as structurally complementary rather than fully substitutable. Fourth, it should bring embodied dignity, demographic renewal, cognitive infrastructure, public integrity, monetary credibility, and temporal fiscal claims into the core of development analysis. Fifth, it should study development indicators not merely as descriptive tools but as governance infrastructures that shape incentives, recognition, and resource allocation. The article concludes by outlining a research programme for Provident Development Studies, including continuity-threshold analysis, cascade-failure mapping, temporal-externality accounting, embodied-dignity diagnostics, and benchmarkgovernance analysis.

title: Algorithms at Exascale: Evaluating AI-Driven Resource Optimization for High-Performance Computing in Large-Scale Scientific Simulations

detail.title: Algorithms at Exascale: Evaluating AI-Driven Resource Optimization for High-Performance Computing in Large-Scale Scientific Simulations
detail.abstract: The advent of exascale computing has introduced a fundamental tension between peak theoretical performance and achievable scientific throughput. Although artificial intelligence has been advanced as a solution for optimizing resource allocation in high-performance computing environments, the empirical evidence supporting such claims remains fragmented and methodologically contested. This paper critically evaluates the efficacy of AI-driven scheduling, power management, and workload placement strategies across three large-scale scientific simulation domains: climate modeling, astrophysics, and molecular dynamics. Drawing on a mixed-methods design that combines quantitative benchmark analysis of 1.2 million job records from a leadership-class facility with qualitative interviews of twenty three computational scientists and system administrators, the study finds that AI optimizers deliver statistically significant improvements in power efficiency (11.4 percent average) and queue time reduction (18.7 percent) but produce negligible gains in scientific throughput measured as simulation time steps completed per watt. Moreover, the analysis reveals a recurrent pattern of performance brittleness: AI models trained on historical workloads degrade substantially when applied to novel simulation campaigns with different memory access patterns or communication topologies. These findings suggest that prevailing AI optimization frameworks optimize for narrow operational metrics rather than the epistemic goals of scientific discovery. The paper contributes a contingency framework that distinguishes between computationally regular and computationally novel workloads, demonstrating that hybrid human-in-the-loop strategies outperform fully automated systems under conditions of scientific exploration. Implications for exascale facility management, algorithm design, and responsible AI deployment in high-stakes computational science are discussed.

title: Governing Control over Human Genetic Resources: Promises and Risks

detail.abstract: The purpose of the paper is to discuss how to regulate the access to and use of biochemical and human genetic material currently considered as part of the market framework. Looking beyond the protection of traditional public goods (such as land or water), the paper emphasizes the debate around the progressive commodification of human genetic resources facilitated by an improper use of intellectual property rights. The discourse around commons is used to evaluate alternative tools and strategies to the issue of private appropriation of human genetic resources and natural compounds

title: Beyond the Star Rating: A National Correlational Analysis of High School Football Player Discovery, Scholarship Attainment, and Division I Production
affiliations: Northcentral University

detail.title: Beyond the Star Rating: A National Correlational Analysis of High School Football Player Discovery, Scholarship Attainment, and Division I Production

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is affiliated with Belleci Group LLC / Recruit Intel, which developed and operates the platform and proprietary data resources discussed in this paper. No other personal or financial conflicts of interest are declared.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve intervention with human participants. The analysis used secondary, source-linked recruiting data and derived variables; no ethics approval was sought or required for this working paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted independently and supported by the author's own resources / Belleci Group LLC.

detail.abstract: College football recruiting decisions for the lower-rated three-star and two-star athletes who populate most Division I rosters have historically rested on third-party star ratings that, in the present data, track recruiting market position (scholarship attainment) far more closely than they track subsequent on-field production. Belleci (2022) examined the relationship between player rating, school scholarship production, and prior team success at the California state level and found that the three-factor framework substantially predicted low-star scholarship attainment. The present study extends that framework nationally and shifts the primary outcome from scholarship attainment to dual outcomes that include both scholarship attainment and Division I statistical production. Grounded in Social Exchange Theory (Blau, 1964; Emerson, 1976; Homans, 1961), the analysis frames recruiting as an exchange relationship in which a third-party ratings layer mediates information flow between coaching staffs and high school student-athletes. The dataset comprises 127,482 recruitable players (classes 2018–2030); a restricted training cohort of graduating classes 2018 through 2022 (n = 22,739, of which 19,555 with offensive linemen excluded) was validated on a 2023–2024 holdout (n = 16,745, of which 14,854 with OL excluded), with a production-linked subset of 6,446 players carrying verified Division I pergame statistics. Analyses employed binary logistic regression, linear regression, Pearson and Spearman correlation, and Cohen's effect-size estimators with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control. The results identify a Scholarship-to-Production Conversion Gap of 44.1 percentage points at the three-star tier (91.5% scholarship attainment versus 47.3% production); the SPCG measures the share of scholarship recipients at each star tier who do not appear in any Division I game during the observation window; it is a structural conversion finding about roster survival, not a direct rating-validity test.

title: A Recurrent Neural-Network Policy for Stochastic Consumption, Investment, and Insurance Optimization
affiliations: , Texas A&M University (TAMU), Central Texas and Texas A&M University Central Texas

detail.title: A Recurrent Neural-Network Policy for Stochastic Consumption, Investment, and Insurance Optimization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no known personal or financial relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study used simulated data and did not involve human participants, patients, or animals.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a customized gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural-network approach for approximating sequential consumption, investment, and insurance decisions under uncertainty. Traditional analytical and dynamic-programming methods provide important benchmarks, but they become difficult to scale as the state space, information structure, or market model increases in complexity. We train the network on simulated return scenarios with target controls generated by a perfect-foresight dynamic-programming benchmark (PFDP), which assumes access to the realized future return path. The learned policy maps observed return history and current wealth to sequential decisions for risky allocation, insurance, and consumption. In held-out rollout evaluations, the GRU-based policy (GBP) remains below the PFDP benchmark, as expected, while achieving a mean utility ratio of approximately 0.942 relative to PFDP in the current experiment. The same evaluation compares the GBP with a causal dynamic-programming baseline (CDP) that resolves the optimization problem at each time step using only currently available information together with a flat extrapolation of future returns. In this setting, the GRU performs favorably against CDP on average. These results support the use of a compact recurrent architecture as a practical approximation framework for sequential financial decision problems while also identifying limitations associated with supervised imitation, simulation assumptions, and numerical approximation. The implementation code, generated results, and plotting scripts are publicly available in the GitHub repository of [Aziz et al., 2026].

title: When Commerce Becomes Conflict: Measuring Geoeconomic Fragmentation Risk
affiliations: CICEE - Research Center in Business & Economics, University of Aveiro - Department of Economics, Management, Industrial Engineering and Tourism, Universidade Católica Portuguesa, Católica Porto Business School and CEGE and CMVM - Comissao do Mercado de Valores Mobiliarios

detail.title: When Commerce Becomes Conflict: Measuring Geoeconomic Fragmentation Risk

keywords: international political economy JEL codes: F13

detail.abstract: The global economy is fragmenting along strategic lines. Trade, finance, technology, and investment are no longer governed solely by efficiency but increasingly by geopolitical rivalry. This paper develops a conceptual and methodological framework for measuring geoeconomic fragmentation risk-the exposure of economies, sectors, and firms to the breakdown, reconfiguration, or strategic restriction of cross-border economic relations. Synthesizing Frank Knight's distinction between measurable risk and genuine uncertainty with Edward Luttwak's theory of geo-economics as strategic conflict through commercial means, the paper proposes a Composite Geoeconomic Fragmentation Risk Index (CGFRI) built from four dimensions: structural vulnerability, policy uncertainty, coercive restriction intensity, and realized fragmentation in trade and investment linkages. The proposed measure draws on publicly available data from LSEG Refinitiv Country Risk Ranking, Trade Policy Uncertainty indices, the World Uncertainty Index, the Global Sanctions Database, the EU Sanctions Map, IMF trade fragmentation indicators, and IMF bilateral direct investment data. The result is a framework that sharpens the concept of geoeconomic fragmentation risk and offers an operational path for empirical testing in corporate finance, international business, and political economy.

title: Interest Rate Environments and Recession Prediction
affiliations: University of Turku, University of Turku - Department of Mathematics and Statistics and University of Turku

detail.title: Interest Rate Environments and Recession Prediction
detail.abstract: Do different interest rate environments affect the predictability of recessions? To address this question, we consider the conventional parametric probit model and nonparametric approaches under different interest rate conditions in the U.S. and the euro area. We find that recession predictability has weakened in both economies as interest rates have declined, and that the estimated coefficients of the probit model are unstable over time, with the term spread coefficient weakening substantially as interest rates fall. In the U.S., the nonparametric approach produces better-calibrated probability forecasts in high-rate environments, most visibly during the 2022--2024 rate hiking episode, when standard probit models signaled recessions that never materialized.

title: An Early Capital Taxation Principle
affiliations: University of Rome Tor Vergata - Department of Economics and Finance and Luiss Guido Carli University - Department of Economics and Finance

detail.title: An Early Capital Taxation Principle
detail.abstract: We reinterpret the classical zero long-run capital tax result as the steady-state implication of a broader intertemporal timing principle. In a standard Ramsey environment, capital and labor taxation are both distortionary instruments, and the planner uses capital taxation to shift distortions across dates by front-loading them relative to labor taxation. The asymptotic disappearance of capital taxation therefore reflects the exhaustion of this intertemporal margin rather than a primitive ranking of fiscal instruments. We substantiate this interpretation through two conceptual experiments. First, restricting government asset accumulation can sustain positive long-run capital taxation. Second, a present-value decomposition of the government's intertemporal budget shows that capital wedges may account for virtually the entire financing of public expenditures even when capital tax rates converge to zero. These results suggest that the Ramsey logic is fundamentally about the optimal sequencing of distortions across time, rather than the long-run superiority of labor taxation.

title: From Enactive Cognition to Co-Constitutive Cognition (C³): The Autopoiesis Paradox and Symbiotic Ontological Reconstruction in Enactive AI

detail.title: From Enactive Cognition to Co-Constitutive Cognition (C³): The Autopoiesis Paradox and Symbiotic Ontological Reconstruction in Enactive AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research was conducted independently, with no financial or personal relationships with any organization that could have influenced the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a theoretical and philosophical study involving no human participants, patient data, clinical trials, or empirical data collection. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was self-funded by the author as part of independent scholarly work conducted under the WorldValue research platform.

detail.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) stall in what this paper terms the "representational dead end"-severing perception from action and generating outputs without genuine agent-environment coupling-Rafiee and Sutton's Enactive AI (2026) offers a timely and important corrective. By elevating reinforcement learning to a philosophy-of-life dimension through four pillars-experience, action-perception inseparability, autonomy, and embodiment-the Enactive AI paradigm marks a genuine advance. This paper engages that paradigm constructively, not as a critic but as a philosophical interlocutor. We identify a precise internal contradiction: Sutton and Rafiee invoke Autopoiesis (Maturana and Varela) to ground Intrinsic Normativity in artificial agents, yet Autopoiesis theory's normative force derives fundamentally from the death threshold-the biological system's ongoing vulnerability to dissolution. Machines lack this threshold; therefore, Autopoiesis loses its ontological engine when transplanted to artificial agents. We name this the Autopoiesis Paradox. Drawing on the author's previously established Process-Paradox Framework (SSRN, January-February 2026) and the Co-Constitutive Paradigm (SSRN, January 2026), we propose Co-Constitutive Cognition (C³) as the missing second-order ontological foundation for Enactive AI. C³'s core thesis is: structure generates cognition, and co-constitution defines the boundary. Intelligence arises not from unstructured interaction alone but from topological structure operating across multiple levels; and the machine's cognitive structure must remain parasitic upon and symbiotic with the death-bound cognitive networks of human individuals to acquire genuine value-anchoring. C³ does not compete with Enactive AI; it completes it; it supplies the ontological groundwork that Enactive AI requires but leaves implicit.

title:
The GEB Framework: Reorienting Artificial Intelligence Toward Growth, Economic Value, and Societal Benefit
A Practitioner-Research Framework for Organisational Leaders

detail.title:
The GEB Framework: Reorienting Artificial Intelligence Toward Growth, Economic Value, and Societal Benefit
A Practitioner-Research Framework for Organisational Leaders
detail.abstract:
Enterprise investment in artificial intelligence has grown at an extraordinary rate over the past decade, yet research consistently indicates that fewer than one in three AI initiatives deliver measurable business outcomes at scale. This paper argues that the dominant model for AI adoption-oriented around technical performance, benchmark superiority, and innovation signalling-is structurally misaligned with the creation of genuine organisational and societal value. Drawing on practitioner experience across Global Capability Centres (GCCs), existing management and technology literature, and observed patterns of AI investment and failure, this paper introduces the GEB Framework: a strategic philosophy and governance model for reorienting AI investment around three interdependent pillars-Growth, Economics, and Building a Better World. 
The paper makes four contributions. First, it diagnoses the structural failure modes that prevent enterprise AI from delivering value. Second, it articulates the three GEB pillars with conceptual clarity and practical specificity. Third, it presents a five-level GEB Maturity Model to help organisations assess their current position and plan a development trajectory. Fourth, it provides a GEB Scorecard-a crosspillar measurement framework-and a phased implementation roadmap for organisations seeking to operationalise GEB principles. The framework is intended to be useful to both organisational leaders making AI investment decisions and to management researchers studying the relationship between AI adoption, business value creation, and societal impact.
